title: Production REST & API Design Standards
summary: Designing predictable, backward-compatible, well-documented APIs that developers love to consume.
keyPrinciples: Consistent URL naming: use plural nouns for resources (`/api/v1/orders`), never verbs.
Standard error formats: adopt RFC 7807 (Problem Details) for machine-readable error responses.
Explicit versioning: never break existing consumers without an explicit deprecation period.

rules.title: Use Standard HTTP Status Codes Semantically
rules.description: Never return `200 OK` with an error message in the JSON body. Use proper 4xx client and 5xx server status codes so clients and caching proxies handle failures correctly.

badExample.explanation: Clients must manually parse every response body to know if the request actually succeeded.

goodExample.explanation: Standardized format readable by any HTTP client library and observability dashboard.

productionChecklist: OpenAPI / Swagger specification generated automatically from code schemas.
Pagination standardized on cursor-based tokens (`cursor` and `limit`) for large collections.
Mutation endpoints support `Idempotency-Key` headers for safe retries.
Rate limits declared via standard headers (`RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`).
